record: the score the reference seals when a local run refuses BEFORE anything ran, so no
CorrectnessReport exists and the golden was never hashed.
CONSTRUCTED FROM THE SWIFT SOURCE, not captured from a box run — the record's every
deterministic field is fixed by the source, and a captured run would only add the wall-clock
noise this fixture deliberately excludes. Derivation, field by field:

only at :152, after the timing pass).

argument, so failedScore's defaults stand.

?? ""` (:1176), checkedSteps `?? 0` (:1161), caseCount

so both passed_*_speedup_floor are 0 >= 0.95 = false;

gpqa_*/semantic_gpqa_*/expert_* and partial_result
take their zero/empty/false defaults.
The three input-shaped values below are TEST INPUTS, not reference facts: `error` is whatever
refusal the caller passes through, and the weights digest triple is whatever the run digested
before it refused (the reference digests the weights at :89, BEFORE the golden load at :101,
so a golden-side refusal still seals a real weights identity). The test feeds exactly these.
The three SECONDS fields (preflight/correctness/timed_benchmark) are substitutable for a THIRD
reason, neither wall-clock-only nor runner identity (#132/F4). They were pinned to a byte-exact
0.0, which is true only for a refusal that happens BEFORE the validation phase closes. The
reference's `failed()` forwards them from live locals --
QwenRuntimeLocalIterate.swift@b26f76f:58   preflightSeconds: validationSeconds,
QwenRuntimeLocalIterate.swift@b26f76f:59   correctnessSeconds: correctnessSeconds,
QwenRuntimeLocalIterate.swift@b26f76f:60   timedBenchmarkSeconds: timedSeconds,
-- and `validationSeconds` is assigned at `:109`, so a refusal reached AFTER that point seals a
NON-ZERO preflightSeconds. The exemplar is the TIMING phase, which starts at `:115`: anything it
throws is caught at `:197-198` with validationSeconds already set. `correctnessSeconds` and
`timedBenchmarkSeconds` come from `timedSeconds` (`:147-150`) and `correctnessSeconds` (`:151`),
both assigned only on the path that got that far.
NOT an exemplar, despite looking like one: the cases-empty guard at `:106-108` THROWS at `:107`,
which is BEFORE `:109`, so validationSeconds is still its `:19` declaration of 0.0 and that
refusal seals ZERO. An earlier draft of this note cited it as the non-zero case, which was
backwards; the substitution is still right, it is the earliest refusals that seal 0.0 and the
later ones that do not.
Pinning 0.0 would therefore assert something false of the reference for every refusal from `:115`
onward. They are substituted rather than dropped: the field must still be PRESENT and numeric,
which is what the substitution loop checks.
`nondeterministic_or_runner_identity` names every field the test substitutes from the actual
payload before comparing. Each is either wall-clock (no fixed value exists on either side) or
a runner-identity label whose benchd-vs-Swift difference is graded elsewhere in
docs/parity-matrix.md — NOT part of what #74 adjudicates. Everything else is compared byte for
byte.
